name: Composer Shell
description: Three-column context-engine workspace shell for the Composer app: left composition-stack rail, center active-layer canvas (progress hairline, layer header, locked-context stack, hosted layer canvas, composer footer, future-preview stack), right files rail. Rails are 0px wide at cold launch and reveal on the first lock / first advance.

evidence.rationale: Identical literal spacing recurs in CompositionStack, FilesRail and ComposerFooter.
Both rail ItemsRepeaters declare StackLayout Spacing=2.
The same Padding literal is declared on both rail panels.

properties.note: applied to LeftRailColumn and RightRailColumn when RailsVisible flips true; 0 otherwise
locked-context card CornerRadius, future-preview card RadiusX/RadiusY, suggestion chip CornerRadius; the declared Corner* resources are not referenced by this surface

evidence.rationale: The same 4px corner recurs across the three card-like surfaces on this shell.
OnLayerRowClick invokes Jump(row.Index); ShellModel.Jump sets ActiveIndex, which is what makes a row render active.
OnPromptTextChanged invokes SetActivePrompt, which calls MarkDirty when the text is non-empty.
OnChipClick writes the chip text into the prompt and invokes SetActivePrompt, which marks the layer dirty.
TriggerPrimary routes the Dirty state to GeneratePreview, which ends by setting the layer state to Previewing.
Both lock commands set the layer to Locked and advance ActiveIndex; RailsVisible is defined as lockedLayers.Count > 0 || ActiveIndex > 0, so the first lock reveals the rails.
DiscardPreview restores the snapshot and sets the layer state back to Clean.
DiscardEdits restores the snapshot and sets the layer state back to Clean.

unresolved.question: Should the eight composition-stack rows and ten file rows be modeled as individual instance nodes rather than one canonical component carrying the item list?
unresolved.reason: Both collections are generated at runtime from the static Layers.All array, so the per-item identity lives in the model rather than the view. The canonical component plus a declared item list captures the same information without eighteen near-identical nodes.

unresolved.question: Where do the active layer's Title and Subtitle actually render now?
unresolved.reason: ActiveLayerHeader still binds Title and Subtitle DPs but its TitleText/SubtitleText TextBlocks are declared Visibility="Collapsed"; a source comment says they moved inside a glass container on the Intent canvas, which is a layer view and out of scope for this graph.

unresolved.question: Is AppTitleRow ever shown, and does its ShowReset binding still have an effect?
unresolved.reason: The instance is declared Visibility="Collapsed" in ActiveCanvas.xaml while still binding ProjectName and HasLockedLayers; no code path in the read sources sets it visible.

unresolved.question: Should the center column be modeled as a navigation region?
unresolved.reason: Comments in Shell.xaml and ActiveCanvas.xaml.cs describe a planned uen:Region.Attached navigation surface with Pages and a RouteMap already registered, but the shipped code hosts canvases directly through CanvasSlot. Only the implemented direct hosting is modeled.

unresolved.question: Do the two synthesized companion rows (README.md and prompt-context.md) ever leave the Planned status?
unresolved.reason: FilesRail.Render always appends them with FileStatus.Planned, and ShellModel.FileStatuses only keys per-layer kinds, so no read source advances them. Note also that the first per-layer file (Intent) is README.md, so the name appears twice in the rail.

unresolved.question: Should the rails-hidden/revealed condition attach to the workspace grid or separately to each rail container?
unresolved.reason: One condition (ShellModel.RailsVisible) drives the column widths on WorkspaceRoot and the opacity/translate of both rail containers simultaneously; the states were attached to the workspace because the column definitions live there, but a per-rail attachment is equally defensible.

unresolved.question: Which of the one-off measurements on this surface represent design rules rather than local values?
unresolved.reason: Recap MaxWidth 560 / LineHeight 20, canvas Padding 32,28,32,40 and Spacing 20, footer CornerRadius 6 and MinHeight 68, and the 480/320/240/160 ms motion timings are all literals in source. Tokens.xaml declares Duration.*, Corner*, Space* and Spacing* resources that this surface never references, so they were deliberately left out of the graph.

metadata.scope: Composer shell surface only. The eight per-layer canvases under Views/Layers are out of scope; the canvas slot records that it hosts them.
metadata.tokenScope: Only values this surface consumes. Unreferenced declarations in Tokens.xaml (phase/state tints, Space*/Spacing*/Corner*/Duration*/easing keys) and Typography.xaml (the fifteen-style v11 scale) were excluded per token-rules.md.
notes: Rail column widths snap between 0 and 280px; only the rail content translate/opacity is animated.
Style-level interaction visuals (StackRowButtonStyle and AmberButtonStyle PointerOver/Pressed/Disabled) were not modeled as states, and their hover shades were not tokenized.
